A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Adam-mini, with identifiable corresponding methods and experiments. All pages, including appendices, equations, tables and figures, support reliable comparison despite substantial revisions.

before.justification: V1 reports original optimization simulations, Transformer Hessian analyses, language-model training and alignment experiments, and vision and graph results.

after.justification: V6 reports original empirical results, including retained training experiments and additional scaling-law studies, Hessian diagnostics and optimizer comparisons.

M1.justification: V1 partitions Query/Key by head, otherwise generally uses whole parameter tensors, and retains coordinate-wise second moments for embedding/output layers. V6 Algorithms 1–3 instead partition embedding/output layers by token and Value/attention-projection/MLP matrices by output neuron, with a whole-Value option for short runs. This substantially changes learning-rate assignments and optimizer storage.

E1.justification: Llama pre-training changes from explicitly processed CommonCrawl 2019-30 data to C4. V6 also adds synthetic binary classification data for the MLP Hessian experiment. OpenWebText, UltraFeedback/MT-Bench, ImageNet, CelebA and OGBN-arxiv tasks remain; the changes are limited within the retained application domains.

E2.justification: V6 adds LAMB to the GPT-2-125M comparison, Adafactor-Zhai-version to Llama comparisons, and Lion evaluations in Appendix C.5. GaLore disappears from the GPT-2-125M comparison, while GaLore and SM3 disappear from the trajectory comparison. These are substantive comparator changes, verified in the corresponding plot legends.

E3.justification: V6 adds controlled scaling runs and 8B/13B evaluations, and reports revised Llama context lengths, batches and a 1% warm-up/linear schedule instead of 2,000-step warm-up/cosine decay. The Transformer Hessian study changes from four layers at initialization to one layer at 1% of training. The reported LoRA learning rate changes from 5e-6 to 2e-5. These are protocol revisions, without independently establishing which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V6 adds MLP Hessian tracking throughout training, controlled matrix-density/preconditioning experiments, scaling analyses, detailed Adafactor/Lion sensitivity sweeps and an AdamW epsilon/loss-spike analysis. V1's layer-by-layer initialization Hessians and exceptional diagonal-block case study are removed or superseded. The trajectory comparison and LoRA analysis already existed in v1, although their reported comparisons are revised.

E5.justification: V6 Appendix E.2 specifies 100 Xavier initializations per matrix and 40 sampled angle configurations per dimension/condition-number pair, averaging results for Figure 5. This adds repeated-sampling estimation for a new diagnostic. It does not establish additional training seeds; the shared-seed trajectory design remains, and neither version provides systematic confidence intervals.

E6.justification: V6 adds scaling results, including 1B-model perplexities of 12.452 for AdamW and 12.372 for Adam-mini after 26.21B tokens (Table 5). Adam-mini's calculated Llama 2-7B optimizer memory changes from 28.04 to 26.96 GB (Table 1). Several training and trajectory curves change, and GPT-2-770M results disappear. MT-Bench and non-LLM table scores remain unchanged; revised experimental conditions preclude interpreting changed curves as same-setting gains.

T1.justification: V6 adds an explicit cross-entropy Hessian expression for a one-hidden-layer network and its assumptions (Equation 1), plus mathematical definitions of matrix density and preconditioning effectiveness (Equation 3). These extend the mathematical reasoning beyond v1's qualitative discussion. The original quadratic construction remains, and no new convergence theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The headline claims change from removing at least 90% of second-moment entries and saving 45–50% memory to removing at least 99.9% and saving 50%. Claimed LLM effectiveness expands from 125M–7B to 39M–13B. The central structural contribution is also revised: Value/MLP blocks previously described as dense wholes are replaced by neuron-level partitions, with token-level embedding/output partitions.

C2.justification: V6 replaces the whole-block and sparse-embedding rationale with token/neuron-level Hessian interpretations and a shared-backpropagation-error explanation for averaging. It adds qualifications about unclear Value structure, training-length-dependent partition choices, untested non-Transformer architectures, baseline tuning and uncertain generalization of the GPT-2 loss-spike finding (Sections 2.3–2.4 and Appendices B–C).

D1.justification: V6 replaces the TinyLlama implementation description with Torchtitan and adds scaling architecture/training tables, runtime information, synthetic-data and matrix-generation code, Hessian ordering instructions and the optimizer.wv_names switch. V1's CommonCrawl preprocessing/split instructions and GaLore configuration are removed. These materially change reproducibility documentation; the Adam-mini repository link itself is retained.

R1.justification: V6 Appendix A adds substantive comparisons with BAGM and NovoGrad, acknowledging earlier block/layer-wise adaptivity and distinguishing Adam-mini's Hessian-based partitions. It also distinguishes LAMB, discusses the relevance and limits of Das et al.'s preconditioning bounds, and substantially expands Hessian-related research positioning. These changes go beyond moving related work or updating citation style.

P1.justification: V6 extensively rewrites the abstract and method narrative, organizes motivation into explicit case studies, and revises the conclusion. Related work, the complete algorithm and non-LLM experiments move into appendices, which are reorganized from A–B into A–E. This substantially changes the document's narrative and organization.

P2.justification: V6 redraws Figure 2, replaces and expands Hessian displays, combines GPT-2 panels, and adds scaling, tuning and instability plots. Memory/throughput tables gain rows and subtables, and new configuration tables appear. Algorithms and LoRA/non-LLM displays are relocated or regrouped, alongside a changed page template and caption styling.

improvement.justification: V6 substantially strengthens validation: the 26.21B-token Llama 2-1B run and scaling study test sustained training, while explicit Adafactor/Lion sweeps address v1's limited baseline-tuning evidence. Revised partition instructions and BAGM/NovoGrad comparisons clarify reproducibility and novelty. These gains outweigh the removed comparisons. A reporting weakness remains: v6's new blanket claim of identical AdamW hyperparameters conflicts with the different ReMax learning rates in Appendix E.1.
